mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that support corporate revenue growth and earnings expansion, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 40% of instances where PAYEMS m/m > 0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation that typically triggers preemptive Federal Reserve tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL y/y > 3.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent month-over-month increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and declines in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate synchronized supply capacity expansion and labor market strength, supporting robust corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO m/m > 0 and UNRATE m/m < 0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and rising), a month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals deteriorating residential demand, which typically precedes broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and FEDFUNDS m/m > 0 and HOUST m/m < 0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in residential sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand for housing, which typically translates to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in less than 40% of instances where RSAFS m/m > 0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent month-over-month increases in industrial production (INDPRO) and year-over-year CPIAUCSL exceeding 3.0% signals economic strength with rising inflation, which typically triggers Federal Reserve rate hikes and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO m/m > 0 and CPIAUCSL y/y > 3.0%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 q/q > 2.0% and UNRATE < 4.0%), a month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening residential demand, which typically foreshadows broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 q/q > 2.0% and UNRATE < 4.0% and HOUST m/m < 0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
